fr.elements: Main Residence; Front Driveway; Access Drive; Detached Structure; Landscaped Area; Open Lawn Area; Dense Vegetation; Retaining Wall; Walkway; Vehicle Parking Area
fr.considerations: Single Access Point; Dense Vegetation; Limited Rear Access; Vegetation Near Structure
fr.recommendations:
• Install a reflective address marker at the driveway entrance so responders can confirm the correct property from the road.
• Mark the single driveway entrance clearly, as it is the only vehicle access point to the property.
• Keep the access drive clear of parked vehicles to allow emergency vehicles to reach the residence and detached structure without obstruction.
• Identify a designated turnaround or staging area on the property and keep it clear, as the single access point limits options for repositioning emergency vehicles.
• Trim dense vegetation along the access drive that may reduce visibility or narrow the passable width for emergency vehicles.
• Cut back dense vegetation growing close to the residence and detached structure so responders can move around both buildings without obstruction.
• Clear a walkable path between the main residence and the detached structure so responders can move quickly between the two buildings.
• Keep any gates along the access drive unlocked or equipped with a lock box to prevent delays when the single access point is blocked by a closed gate.
• Mark or make visible any retaining wall edges near the driveway or access drive so responders moving in low-light conditions can identify drop-offs.
• Communicate to responding units in advance that rear access to the property is limited, requiring all approach and staging from the front driveway.

wildfire.conditions: Structure Surrounded by Vegetation; Tree Cluster; Tree Cluster; Scattered Trees; Vegetation Near Structure; Vegetation Near Structure; Scattered Shrubs; Ground Vegetation; Open Green Space; Limited Vegetation Separation; Single Access Route; Grass Cover
wildfire.recommendations:
• Trim tree branches that hang directly over or touch the roof and exterior walls of the structure.
• Thin the dense tree clusters near the structure to create open gaps between individual trees.
• Remove shrubs growing directly against the foundation and exterior walls.
• Cut back or remove shrubs and ground vegetation within the immediate area surrounding the structure.
• Mow or cut the grass cover close to the structure to reduce the amount of low-lying material that can carry fire toward the building.
• Separate scattered shrubs from nearby trees by removing shrubs positioned directly beneath tree canopies.
• Clear any dead leaves, branches, or plant debris that has collected against the structure's walls, under decks, or in corners.
• Thin scattered trees near the structure so their canopies do not touch or overlap with each other.
• Keep the single access route clear of overhanging branches and encroaching vegetation on both sides so emergency vehicles can pass without obstruction.
• Remove vegetation growing along the edges of the access route that has grown into the travel lane or reduced the usable width of the road.
• Maintain the open green space by keeping grass mowed short, particularly in areas closest to the structure.
• Move any woodpiles, stored materials, or other flammable items away from the structure's exterior walls and store them at a distance.
